record.paper_title: Open Problems in Hydrodynamical Approach to Relativistic Heavy Ion Collisions
record.original_question: What practical covariant formulation of relativistic dissipative hydrodynamics can preserve causal signal propagation, avoid the acausal thermal-current behavior of the Landau formulation, and avoid the many unknown parameters, higher time derivatives, extra initial-condition difficulties, and numerical complications associated with the Israel-Stewart-Miller second-order theory?

evidence.quote: However, a covariant theory of dissipative phenomena is not trivial at all. We know that the diffusion equation is not covariant, and the equation is parabolic so that the propagation of signal has an infinite velocity.

However, this theory is too general and complex, containing many unknown parameters which make difficult the application of the theory to practical problems. Furthermore, the theory contains the third order time derivatives, introducing additional difficulties of initial value problem and numerical procedure.
Because of the simple form of viscous terms, incorporation of these equations to the realistic hydro-code such as SPHERIO is relatively easy. A work on this line is in progress.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a relativistic fluid on Minkowski (or curved) spacetime with energy-momentum tensor and conserved currents that admit dissipative corrections (shear viscosity, bulk viscosity, heat conduction). The Landau–Lifshitz first-order formulation leads to parabolic equations and superluminal signal propagation (acausal heat/diffusion currents), while the Israel–Stewart–Müller second-order theory restores causality at the price of introducing many phenomenological relaxation parameters, third-order time derivatives in the equations of motion, additional initial-value data, and numerical stiffness.

Problem: Construct a covariant formulation of relativistic dissipative hydrodynamics that simultaneously satisfies all of the following:

1. The system of evolution equations is hyperbolic, with all characteristic speeds bounded by the speed of light, so that signal propagation is causal.
2. Equilibrium states are linearly (and ideally nonlinearly) stable in every Lorentz frame.
3. The theory incorporates shear viscosity, bulk viscosity, and heat conduction, reducing to the appropriate Navier–Stokes-type behavior in the slow-evolution limit.
4. The equations are at most second order in derivatives of the hydrodynamic fields and do not require the introduction of independent dissipative tensors as new dynamical variables with their own relaxation equations and unknown transport parameters beyond the standard ones.
5. The formulation is amenable to direct implementation in realistic numerical hydrodynamic codes without the initial-condition and stiffness complications of Israel–Stewart–Müller theory.

Find such a formulation, or prove that no formulation satisfying all of the above conditions exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem has been largely resolved by the Bemfica–Disconzi–Noronha–Kovtun (BDNK) framework, which provides a first-order covariant formulation of relativistic viscous hydrodynamics that is causal, strongly hyperbolic, and linearly/nonlinearly stable under explicit constraints on transport coefficients, including shear and bulk viscosity, heat conduction, and coupling to Einstein's equations. The theory avoids the auxiliary dissipative variables and higher-derivative complications of Israel–Stewart–Müller theory and has been implemented in numerical simulations. Subsequent works have extended the formulation to anisotropic hydrodynamics, magnetohydrodynamics, and ideal-gas microphysics.

status_evidence.title: First-Order General-Relativistic Viscous Fluid Dynamics (Bemfica, Disconzi, Noronha)
status_evidence.snippet: First generalization of Navier-Stokes theory to relativity that is causal, strongly hyperbolic, stable, and includes shear viscosity, bulk viscosity, and thermal conductivity, in the nonlinear regime.
status_evidence.claim: A first-order covariant dissipative hydrodynamics has been constructed that is causal, stable, and includes all leading dissipative effects without the complications of Israel–Stewart theory.

status_evidence.title: Causal, stable first-order viscous relativistic hydrodynamics with ideal gas microphysics
status_evidence.snippet: BDNK theory offers a practical and straightforward approach to address the long-standing issues of causality, stability, and local well-posedness in relativistic fluids.
status_evidence.claim: The BDNK formulation provides a practical, causal first-order alternative to Israel–Stewart–Müller theory suitable for numerical implementation.

status_evidence.title: Nonlinear causality of general first-order relativistic viscous hydrodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: First-order theories can be causal and stable using hydrodynamic fields defined differently from Eckart and Landau-Lifshitz.
status_evidence.claim: Causality and stability are achievable in first-order relativistic viscous hydrodynamics with appropriate frame choices.
